---
title: "Mini-dictator Classroom Results"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
    orientation: rows
    scrolling: true
resources:
  - app.js
  - data/public_results.json
  - data/public_manifest.json
---

```{=html}
<div id="dashboardApp" class="dashboard-shell" aria-live="polite">
  <section class="hero-panel">
    <div>
      <p class="eyebrow">CLASSROOM EXPLORATION</p>
      <h1>Mini-dictator behaviour dashboard</h1>
      <p class="hero-copy">Compare the class snapshot with the international reference sample. All interactions happen in your browser.</p>
    </div>
    <div id="publicationMeta" class="publication-meta">Loading the published snapshot…</div>
  </section>

  <div id="dataStatus" class="status-banner" role="status">Loading data…</div>

  <section class="method-note">
    <strong>How to read these results:</strong>
    Altruist, Egalitarian, Selfish and Antisocial are overlapping indicators, not mutually exclusive categories.
    One participant may appear in two indicators, so their percentages may add to more than 100%.
    Small cells are hidden to protect privacy.
  </section>

  <section class="control-panel" aria-label="Dashboard filters">
    <label>Reference country
      <select id="countrySelect"></select>
    </label>
    <label>Gender
      <select id="genderSelect">
        <option value="all">All respondents</option>
        <option value="female">Female</option>
        <option value="male">Male</option>
      </select>
    </label>
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Behaviours</legend>
      <div id="behaviourControls" class="check-grid"></div>
    </fieldset>
  </section>

  <section class="sample-grid" aria-label="Sample sizes">
    <article class="metric-card"><span>Class complete responses</span><strong id="classComplete">—</strong></article>
    <article class="metric-card"><span>Class consistent responses</span><strong id="classConsistent">—</strong></article>
    <article class="metric-card"><span>Reference complete responses</span><strong id="referenceComplete">—</strong></article>
    <article class="metric-card"><span>Reference consistent responses</span><strong id="referenceConsistent">—</strong></article>
  </section>

  <section class="comparison-grid">
    <article class="chart-card">
      <div class="card-heading"><div><p class="eyebrow">CLASS</p><h2>Our group</h2></div><span class="denominator-help">Behaviour denominator: consistent responses</span></div>
      <div id="classBars" class="bar-chart"></div>
    </article>
    <article class="chart-card">
      <div class="card-heading"><div><p class="eyebrow">REFERENCE</p><h2 id="referenceTitle">International sample</h2></div><span class="denominator-help">Behaviour denominator: consistent responses</span></div>
      <div id="referenceBars" class="bar-chart"></div>
    </article>
  </section>

  <section class="table-card">
    <div class="card-heading"><div><p class="eyebrow">DETAIL</p><h2>Comparison table</h2></div></div>
    <div class="table-scroll">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Behaviour</th><th>Class count</th><th>Class %</th><th>Reference count</th><th>Reference %</th><th>Denominator</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody id="comparisonTable"></tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="matrix-card">
    <div class="card-heading matrix-heading">
      <div><p class="eyebrow">CONSISTENT RESPONSES</p><h2>Compassion × envy map</h2></div>
      <label>Sample
        <select id="matrixScope"><option value="class">Class</option><option value="international">Reference</option></select>
      </label>
    </div>
    <p class="matrix-explainer">Rows show compassion level (low to high); columns show envy level (low to high). Values are shares of consistent responses.</p>
    <div class="matrix-layout">
      <span class="matrix-y-label">Higher compassion ↑</span>
      <div id="matrixGrid" class="matrix-grid"></div>
      <span class="matrix-x-label">Higher envy →</span>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="discussion-card">
    <p class="eyebrow">DISCUSS</p>
    <h2>Questions for the classroom</h2>
    <ol>
      <li>Which differences between the class and the reference sample are largest?</li>
      <li>How does the selected gender filter change the comparison?</li>
      <li>Why can the four behaviour percentages add to more than 100%?</li>
      <li>Which conclusions are not justified when a value is suppressed or a sample is small?</li>
    </ol>
  </section>
</div>
<script src="app.js"></script>
```
